Subject: Private deployment upgrade: pin/unpin handback and rollback ladder

Hi Alex / FinHealth ops,

Following our workshop last week I put together a concise upgrade runbook for your Private deployment (VPC) that balances a short maintenance window with clear escape hatches. Please find the draft attached (upgrade-plan-v2.pdf) and the network diagram for the proposed canary slice. High level: 

- Goal: move cluster from v1.14.2 -> v1.15.0 with minimal customer impact and a tested rollback ladder.
- Proposed window: Sat 2026-09-04 02:00 - 06:00 UTC (overnight for your region).
- Pin/unpin approach: pin control-plane to v1.14.2 until after canary traffic validation; unpin staged pools after successful bake.
- Rollback ladder: (1) abort and restore pinned pool config; (2) evict canary and route traffic to standby pool; (3) full-shelve and emergency rollback to snapshot image.

Open questions for you: 
1) Can you confirm the allowed blackout windows for FinHealth scheduled work?
2) Any regulatory freeze periods in September we should avoid?

Attachments referenced here: upgrade-plan-v2.pdf (runbook), network-diagram-aug21.png. I created a shared Drive folder with the runbook and the verification checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-upgrade-plan

Next steps I propose: 1) internal ops rehearsal week of 2026-08-24, 2) customer canary on 2026-09-04, 3) broad rollout week of 2026-09-11 if green.

If that schedule works for FinHealth, I can publish the final runbook and DocuSign the maintenance acknowledgement.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priyom,

Thanks for the doc — looks thorough. A few notes from our side: 

- The proposed window Sep 4 is OK from a business standpoint, but we have a nightly job at 04:30 UTC that must finish before any control-plane evictions. Can you confirm the canary validation will avoid that time or hold traffic?
- We require a documented rollback SLA: if the canary fails validation within 30 minutes, we expect a fully automated path to restore the previous image within 45 minutes.
- Our security/compliance team needs the list of audit events that will be produced during the pin/unpin and the retention policy for those logs.

Also, can you confirm whether the network-diagram includes the peered audit VPC? I couldn't locate it in the image.

If you can address the three bullets I can loop in our infra ops lead to sign off.

Alex
Ops Manager, FinHealth
alex.teller@finhealth.com

Alex / team,

Thanks — answering the checklist directly below. Quoting key asks: 

> - canary avoids nightly job at 04:30 UTC
> - rollback SLA: restore previous image within 45 minutes
> - list of audit events and retention

Technical responses (short):
1) Canary timing: we will schedule the canary slice validation from 03:00 - 03:30 UTC (before your 04:30 job). Canary will receive a mirrored, low-rpm traffic profile; traffic routing is via our smart-routing policy and can be paused instantly.

2) Rollback SLA: automated rollback path exists for the canary using snapshot images + control-plane pin. Steps:
   - Step A: immediately unroute canary (instant, < 30s)
   - Step B: trigger pin restore (re-apply pinned manifest) — automated script takes ~10-20 minutes depending on image registry throughput
   - Step C: run sanity probes and re-open traffic.

Meeting the 45 minute SLA in all cases requires 1) pre-warmed standby node images in the same region and 2) registry acceleration (we recommend enabling our registry-mirror on your airgapped node). If FinHealth can pre-warm snapshots we'll comfortably meet 45 mins; otherwise worst-case could be ~60 mins.

3) Audit events: the platform emits these events during upgrades: upgrade.start, canary.bake.status, node.eviction, manifest.apply, rollback.initiated, rollback.completed. We will export the events to your audit VPC (pubsub -> s3) and retain for 180 days by default; we can extend retention to 365 days if needed. I'll add a table of event names and sample JSON payloads to the runbook.

Additional ops notes: 
- Network: the attached network-diagram-aug21.png has a smaller callout for the audit VPC; I'll update it to include the peering CIDR and cross-account role.
- Backout criteria: any end-to-end error rate > 3% on the canary for 15 consecutive minutes triggers automatic rollback.

Will run an internal dry-run Thursday 2026-08-26 and invite FinHealth observers so you can validate timings.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
